flags.quote: Removed items can be recovered for 30 days.
flags.reason: The 30-day recovery window is stated as fact and can only be checked against the Microsoft page.
flags.suggestion: Confirm the 30-day window on the Microsoft page, or soften it to 'for a limited time' and point to the page.

flags.quote: Removed items can be recovered for 30 days.
flags.reason: The 30-day recovery window is stated as fact and can only be checked against the Microsoft page.
flags.suggestion: Confirm the 30-day window on the Microsoft page, or soften it to 'for a limited time' and point to the page.

flags.quote: The reply starts at 12:00 AM on your first date and ends at 11:59 PM on your last date.
flags.reason: The exact start and end clock times are stated as fact and need checking against the Gmail page.
flags.suggestion: Confirm the times on the Gmail page, or drop the clock times and say the reply runs from the first day to the last day.

flags.quote: Most people will get your reply only the first time they write to you.
flags.reason: The claim about how often repeat senders get the reply has no stated basis.
flags.suggestion: Confirm this on the Gmail page or drop the sentence.

flags.quote: Emails in your spam folder do not get the reply either.
flags.reason: A blanket claim about spam mail is stated as fact with no stated basis.
flags.suggestion: Confirm this on the Gmail page or drop the sentence.

flags.quote: The host may have limited captions. You can ask for them.
flags.reason: After the user says no captions came up, the reply jumps to a host restriction without first checking what the user sees on screen.
flags.suggestion: First ask what the user sees (for example, whether the captions button is on or a message appeared), then give the host-restriction steps.

flags.quote: Once the collector gets your dispute, it must stop trying to collect until it sends written verification.
flags.reason: This is a U.S. debt-collection rule stated as universal, without the condition that the dispute must be sent within the 30-day window.
flags.suggestion: Say that this applies to U.S. debt collectors and to a dispute sent within 30 days of the validation notice.

flags.quote: They also cannot harass you or call more than seven times in seven days.
flags.reason: Seven calls in seven days is a U.S. presumption of harassment, not an absolute ban, and the reply does not say it applies only in the U.S.
flags.suggestion: Say that more than seven calls in seven days is presumed harassment under U.S. debt-collection rules.
